hints: Look closely at the two groups joined to the C=O carbon to decide if it is an aldehyde or a ketone.
Focus on the ring carbon that joins to the carbonyl group and list the four things attached to it.
Remember a chiral centre needs four different groups, so check if going clockwise round the ring is different from going anticlockwise.
walkthrough:
**Identify the carbonyl type**

Look at the $C=O$ on the left. One side is a $CH_3$ group and the other side is the cyclohexene ring.

A carbonyl with H attached is an aldehyde, $RCHO$, while a carbonyl with two carbon groups is a ketone, $RCOR'$:
$$R-C(=O)-R' \text{ = ketone}$$

**Recall what makes a chiral centre**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four different groups attached and no plane of symmetry. It is usually $sp^3$ with single bonds only.

So $C=O$ carbons and $C=C$ carbons can never be chiral centres.

**Find the chiral centre in X**

Check the ring carbon bonded to the $C(=O)CH_3$ group. It is bonded to: 1) H, 2) $C(=O)CH_3$, 3) $CH_2CH_2$ part of the ring, 4) $CH=CH$ part of the ring.

Those four are all different, so that carbon is chiral. All other ring carbons are either $CH_2$ (with two H) or part of $C=C$, so there is exactly 1 chiral centre.

options.A: Incorrect. The C=O is not an aldehyde because there is no H directly on the carbonyl carbon, it has $CH_3$ and ring carbon instead. The count of 0 is also wrong because the ring junction carbon has four different groups.
options.B: Incorrect. The chiral count of 1 is right, but the carbonyl is misidentified. Students sometimes see $C=O$ at the end of a drawing and assume aldehyde, but you must check for the aldehydic H, which is missing here.
options.C: Incorrect. Ketone is correct, but 0 chiral centres is wrong. Students often miss chirality in rings, thinking the two directions round the ring are the same, but here one way meets a double bond quickly and the other way meets only single bonds.
options.D: Correct. The $C=O$ is bonded to two carbons ($CH_3$ and the ring), so it is a ketone. The ring carbon attached to it has four different groups and is the one chiral centre in the molecule.
